description: Table iteration order, length and the table library. MoonSharp's pairs order is insertion order (docs/ROADMAP.md decisions, 2026-10-28); a key set to nil is forgotten at the next insert of a new key.

cases.name: pairs: constructor puts named fields before positional ones
cases.source: local r = {} for k in pairs({ 10, 20, 30, x = 1, y = 2 }) do r[#r + 1] = tostring(k) end return r

cases.name: pairs: string keys in insertion order
cases.source: local t = {} t.b = 1 t.a = 2 t.c = 3 t.z = 4 t.m = 5 local r = {} for k in pairs(t) do r[#r + 1] = k end return r
cases.note: Lua 5.2 uses hash order: m a z c b

cases.name: pairs: mixed key types in insertion order
cases.source: local t = {} t.b = 1 t[1] = 1 t.a = 1 t[3] = 1 t[2] = 1 t[true] = 1 t[1.5] = 1 local r = {} for k in pairs(t) do r[#r + 1] = tostring(k) end return r

cases.name: pairs: a removed and re-inserted key moves to the end
cases.source: local t = { a = 1, b = 2, c = 3 } t.b = nil t.d = 4 t.b = 5 local r = {} for k in pairs(t) do r[#r + 1] = k end return r

cases.name: pairs: clearing a field during traversal
cases.source: local t = { a = 1, b = 2, c = 3, d = 4 } local seen = {} for k in pairs(t) do seen[#seen + 1] = k if k == 'b' then t.c = nil end end local after = {} for k in pairs(t) do after[#after + 1] = k end return { seen, after }

cases.name: pairs: array part after holes
cases.source: local t = { 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 } t[2] = nil t[4] = nil local r = {} for k in pairs(t) do r[#r + 1] = k end return r

cases.name: pairs: out-of-order integer keys
cases.source: local t = {} for i = 1, 5 do t[i] = i end t[7] = 7 t[6] = 6 local r = {} for k in pairs(t) do r[#r + 1] = k end return { r, #t }

cases.name: pairs: constructor with explicit integer keys
cases.source: local t = { [3] = 'c', 'a', 'b', [10] = 'j', k = 'k' } local r = {} for k in pairs(t) do r[#r + 1] = tostring(k) end return { r, #t }

cases.name: pairs: keys added after clearing every field
cases.source: local t = { 1, 2, 3, a = 1 } for k in pairs(t) do t[k] = nil end t.z = 1 t[1] = 1 local r = {} for k in pairs(t) do r[#r + 1] = tostring(k) end return r
cases.note: storing z forgets every cleared key, so 1 is new again; before the dead-key fix only the first one (a) was forgotten and 1 kept its place

cases.name: length: borders with holes
cases.note: Any border is valid; Lua 5.2 gives 5, 4, 1, 3, 0

cases.name: ipairs stops at the first nil
cases.source: local r = {} for _, v in ipairs({ 1, 2, nil, 4 }) do r[#r + 1] = v end return r

cases.name: next on empty and non-empty tables
cases.source: return { next({}) == nil, next({ 5 }) }

cases.name: numeric string keys differ from numbers
cases.source: local t = {} t['1'] = 'str' t[1] = 'num' return { t['1'], t[1] }

cases.name: table.insert and table.remove
cases.source: local t = { 1, 2, 3 } table.insert(t, 4) table.insert(t, 1, 0) local last = table.remove(t) local first = table.remove(t, 1) return { t, last, first }

cases.name: table.sort with and without a comparator
cases.source: local t = { 5, 2, 8, 1, 9, 3 } table.sort(t) local u = { 'b', 'a', 'C' } table.sort(u, function(a, b) return a:lower() < b:lower() end) return { t, u }

cases.name: table.sort rejects an inconsistent comparator
cases.source: local t = { 3, 1, 2 } table.sort(t, function() return true end) return t

expectError.messageContains: tables.lua:(1,32-63): invalid order function for sorting

cases.note: Lua 5.2 sorts without an error here

cases.name: table.unpack and select use the border
cases.source: return { select('#', table.unpack({ 1, nil, 3 })), select(2, 'a', 'b', 'c'), select(-1, 'a', 'b'), select('#') }

cases.name: rawlen and rawequal
cases.source: return { rawlen({ 1, 2 }), rawlen('abc'), rawequal('a', 'a'), rawequal({}, {}) }

cases.name: error: NaN key
cases.source: local t = {} t[0/0] = 1

cases.name: error: nil key
cases.source: local t = {} t[nil] = 1

cases.name: json.serialize object key order follows pairs
cases.source: local t = {} t.b = 1 t.a = 2 t.c = 3 return json.serialize(t)

cases.name: json.serialize writes a table with 1..n and string keys as an object
cases.source: local t = {} t.b = 1 t.a = 2 t[1] = 3 return json.serialize(t)
